blocks.text: The question about tribute to Caesar is posed as an attempt to trap Jesus (vv. 15-18), not as a neutral request for advice. It belongs to a remembered first-century setting shaped by Roman authority, Herodian client rule, taxation, and elite power. Many scholars date Matthew roughly 70–100 CE, often after Jerusalem’s temple destruction, though the text itself gives no exact date. The Gospel also distinguishes this tribute-to-Caesar controversy from its separate temple-tax scene, so the issues should not simply be treated as identical.

In verses 34-40, Jesus places wholehearted love of God alongside love of one’s neighbor and says that the law and the prophets depend on these commands. This summary cannot legitimately be used to excuse abuse, stigmatize disability or mental illness, enforce misogyny or anti-LGBTQ harm, blame poverty, set apocalyptic dates, or map ancient judgments onto modern peoples.
